nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ whose subgroup lattice is complemented (a $K$-group) with a normal subgroup $N$ whose own subgroup lattice is not complemented; so Kourovka Problem 11.128 has a negative answer.
nodes.title: Normal subgroups of $K$-groups need not be $K$-groups

nodes.summary: Call a group $G$ a $K$-group when its subgroup lattice is complemented: every subgroup $A$ of $G$ has a subgroup $B$ with $A \cap B = 1$ and $\langle A, B \rangle = G$. This is the assertion (M. Emaldi) that every normal subgroup of a $K$-group, viewed as a group in its own right, is again a $K$-group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.128 on normal subgroups of $K$-groups
